sentences.text: I'm in our office in Charlotte Street.
Ah, nice.
This meeting is being recorded.
Working from home today in Somerset.
Somerset, okay.
Very nice.
Part of the world.
It is not bad.
It's probably one of the wettest places on the planet, but today is not too bad.
So.
And do you come up to London much or you tend to do most of your work from home?
Yeah, we're probably in London every week.
Every other week, something like that.
I do a lot of work from home, but my team is, is distributed internationally.
So yeah, we're in the Middle east and across America.
So yeah, so it's all work from remotes really.
But yeah, we're based on Hanover Square, so Marylebone area.
Okay.
Not so bad at all.
Yeah, pretty good.
Well, thank you for your time today and thank you for getting in touch.
These calls really just sort of find out what it is that you're looking to do and see if we can help you at all.
It looks like you guys are in the process of trying to acquire some agencies.
Yeah, I mean we're interested in people who are providing CX experience digital services providers across really first party data.
That's where we kind of operate.
Okay, cool.
You know, using external technologies as well as in house technologies to basically bring all first party data to the same place to better target brands.
We do that for large clients.
You know, we've got some big names and so really we want more of the same.
We do it on a global basis.
60% of our revenues come out of the US about 9% in Australia and just under 30% in Europe in the UK.
So yeah, anything of that ilk really.
We're a listed company so we have currency in terms of we can issue capitala to purchase companies if we need to.

That is not always the case and wouldn't suit everybody but really we're looking for, you know, customers and clients, USPs, companies that have got to a certain point where they can't really grow much more without significant introductions of capitala, you know, in that kind of Fortune 500 large company target market in reality.
Okay, all right.
So it was, wasn't massively obvious with the, the note that you, you sent on our, on our form.
So.
So Silver Bullet is a listed company and what's the size of the business?
So we'll turn over around £10 million this year.
Okay.
All right.
So you said annual revenue 1 to 3.
So are you looking for businesses that are doing annual revenue to 1 and 3 million?
Is that the sweet spot?
I think so, yeah.
I mean I would Never ignore anything in reality because if you turn around and say We've got a 20 million pound turnover business, are you interested in it?
Of course I'd be interested in it.
But that might be slightly more difficult to acquire given that the relative size of our business and the size of that business.
Yeah, you know, and I think probably at that size is when businesses tend to struggle to go much bigger than that.
So the opportunity to consolidate something in a more straightforward manner is in that area.
But I wouldn't exclude anything in reality.
Yeah.
Okay, so just forgive my sort of lack of knowledge in the, in the area that you're in.
So you're saying that you, you're looking for cx.
So what, what exactly is that?
It's customer experience.
Is it?
Yeah.
And what does that mean to, to you as a business?
Customer experience.
So is, is that you're looking for companies that help their clients to improve the customer experience during.
What is that like experience with their digital assets or.
Yes, with their digital assets that drives more success with their brands because of insights that we give them from the use of their data.
I mean you find a lot of companies have data related to their customers, but they don't know how to connect all the dots together and we're quite good at that.
Okay, so is this client's, These would tend to be brands and basically your.
What.
How do you track all of that with the first party data?
Tracking.
Is that because you have your own properties or are you tracking that?
We have a.
We have our own.
Yeah, we have our own data models and we also use third party data models as well.

And we just have deep expertise in taking disparate groups of data and helping customers, you know, drive them through implementing loyalty brands and things like that that help them better target their audience and ultimately help drive their revenues.
Okay, so you're looking for other companies that offer the same services as you do.
Yeah.
In reality.
Or are complementary from a client perspective, from a geography perspective or from a skill set perspective.
If somebody's doing something in first party data that's different to what we're doing, it may well be complementary.
And what I mean by that is they might be, I don't know, think of a stupid example.

You know, there might be somebody who is taking a customer's first party data and doing some kind of fancy marketing that you know is leading edge and using some kind of AI technology that, you know, we're not aware of.
Well, we'd be interested in that because that's complementary to what we do okay.
All right, so in terms of the size of these business, so 1,3 million revenue and EBITDA of around 500k.
So those are relatively small businesses.
Yeah, I guess.
Are they startups or they just haven't they, they kind of failed to, to grow past a, a ceiling and they may be legacy businesses or.
Yeah, I, I, I think what you find is, you know, there may well be some lifestyle businesses that have gone to a certain point and they can't go any further and they don't want to go any further.

There may be some businesses that started up five years ago, they're ready to go to the next stage, but they don't know how to go to the next stage in terms of, you know, they don't necessarily have the M and A experience and don't know how to, you know, increase their business from growing 5 or 10% per annum to doubling it.
So, you know, you quite often find businesses of that size that are ready to make the next move, but don't quite know how to make the next move.
Yeah, true, Yeah.
I mean this is our specialty, this market and certainly at the lower end, sort of sub 20 million revenue businesses, we're probably, our expertise definitely lies between 1 and 20 million.
And are these mostly in the US you're looking for?
Because you're talking about geography.
I guess you're based in the UK and you said a lot of your work is coming from the US already.
So are you looking to just expand more boots on the ground out there?
Is that the idea?
I mean, I think that's if you look at the way the market is and the way the world is, I mean that's where most of the spend is and where most of the opportunity is.
But again, I wouldn't exclude any geographies per se, but the US market ultimately is the biggest market in the world and it is the one that is growing the most rapidly.

So you know, logically you would expect more opportunities to be there, particularly as well the way that commerce works in the US in terms of there are lots of these kinds of boutiques around, you know, that's what the US economy is built off.
So I would expect there are more opportunities there than say in the UK or you know, certain parts of Europe.

But again, I wouldn't exclude anything certainly in the US and Emea Asia pack's more problematical because clearly you've got a logistical issue in the first place and there are business practices in certain parts of the world that are difficult to deal with as well.
So yeah, I would certainly expect most of the opportunities that you see come from the US Market in this kind of space.
But again, I wouldn't exclude anything in this part of the world either.
It really comes down to who they have as clients, their footprint, and what they're offering.
Okay, so what are you doing at the moment then?
Are you.
Are you currently doing outreach to.
To bring more deals in for yourself?
I. I've got a bit of.
A bit of history and background in M and A anyway, so I've got one or two people I'm talking to and.
But I don't have a formal mandate with anybody because touch with one or two people and say, you know, let me know if you've got anything that you think might be of interest.
Okay.
So what's the sort of pace of your acquisitions?
Have you completed any so far?
Yeah, we did one at the end of last year.
We looked at a much bigger1 in Q1, Q2 that would have involved delisting somebody.
And at the end of the day, we decided not to proceed with that.
So I'm looking at another opportunity at the moment.
But again, I think in this kind of activity, you need to have.
It's a bit like a sales pipeline.
You need to have, you know, half a dozen deals on the go to pull one off successfully.
So, you know, the pipeline definitely needs to be filled up more than it currently is.
Okay, cool.
All right, so look, we obviously have the platform agencies, which is, I think, where you've.
You've come free.
So agencies is our platform for buyers and sellers, and we list agencies as they come up for sale there.
So certainly the first port of call would be to sign up to our mailing list and make sure that you get those in your inbox.
But we also work as capitala A on the buy side, as buy side advisory.
And really where our specialty lies is being able to scale up that outbound and give our clients the volume to make multiple acquisitions.
So for instance, we've been working with skyview for just over a year, and they've just closed their third acquisition with us.
So we've really helped them to go from a standing start.
They had no experience in marketing services and had made acquisitions previously to working with us.
And like I say, it's 12 months since their first acquisition.
They've just closed their third with us.
So what we really do is help our clients to get in front of lots and lots of opportunities, have lots of conversations, and just keep that deal pipeline flowing through.
We also help any way that we're needed with requests for information and due diligence, et cetera, et cetera.
It's really soup to nuts on the MA side.
But we do work with lots of experienced guys like you who kind of just really need us to get the deals, the door and we do all of the upfront conversations.
So we will do the screening call and then set it up and we provide you with a one sheeter.
So, you know, if these are people that aren't really interested in selling, we'll just filter them out.
If they want to sell or they're interested in having a conversation, then we set up those, those calls with you with that one sheeter.
So you've got all the information.
That first call really is really straightforward for you.
You don't have to do any research and they are basically selling themselves.
And then once you've had that first call, like I say, we help with requests for further information and really just getting the deal over the line.
Quite often we will have a sidebar conversation with the seller.
Sort of off record to nudge things along.

Being agency people ourselves, we have a lot of senior advisors working in our team or basically agency previously experienced it as agency owners or as C suite agency people who have worked within an acquisition, whether they've sold and been part of a team that's sold or whatever.
So really experienced team, particularly in the US as well.
We've got some great people over there.
I don't know if that's something you're looking for.
It sounds like you're just keeping in touch with a load of brokers at this stage.
But certainly I'm happy to give you more information on that if you want it.
Feel free to send me something through and I'll have a look at it.
I need to see where we get to on the deal we're doing at the moment.
And then, you know, probably beginning next year anyway, I'll probably have a little bit more capacity and a bit more of a plan anyway and a bit more structured to the plan.
So, yeah, you would need a lot of time in your hands because we'll be giving you three or four meetings a week most weeks, which I appreciate, not everybody has the time to that.
I'll send you that over.
Yeah.
Basically the model is a retainer and then a small win fee on the deal.
Okay, excellent.
All right, cool, I'll send that over.
All right, brilliant.
Well, nice to meet you.
Good to meet you, Chris.
Thank you.
Yeah, speak soon.
Have a great day.
You too.
Bye.

summary.overview:
- Andy Day works remotely from Somerset, collaborating with a diverse international team in the US, UK, and Middle East.
- Silver Bullet, a listed company, anticipates a turnover of £10 million this year, focusing on acquiring customer experience and digital services agencies.
- Target acquisition size ranges from £1-3 million in revenue, with interest in larger firms up to £20 million turnover, specifically those offering CX data-driven services.
- Most acquisition opportunities are projected in the US market, which presents significant size and growth potential for Silver Bullet.
- The current M&A pipeline is limited; one acquisition was closed last year, with ongoing discussions for potential targets.
- CapitalA provides essential services including buyer/seller listings, advisory on acquisitions, and support in due diligence processes.
- Chris Ellis intends to review current deal progress before formal engagement with CapitalA for potential acquisitions.
- Plans to increase the volume of buyer meetings are being considered, with a retainer plus success fee model for CapitalA's services.
- The meeting emphasized the importance of expanding the acquisition pipeline, with structured plans anticipated for the following year.
summary.short_summary: The company is pursuing growth through acquisitions of digital customer experience (CX) agencies specializing in first-party data services, predominantly in the US market, which accounts for 60% of its revenue. Chris highlighted the focus on businesses generating between £1 million and £3 million in revenue, with an EBITDA of around £500k, as these companies often plateau without capital. The strategy includes targeting firms with complementary skills, especially those utilizing advanced AI marketing techniques. While the US market is prioritized due to its growth potential, opportunities in Europe and Australia are also being explored. The company maintains a modest pace in acquisitions, having completed one deal last year and declining a larger potential deal this year for strategic reasons. Partnerships are being sought to enhance acquisition outreach and improve deal flow, with financial planning aimed at accelerating acquisition efforts in the near future.
